courseTitle: Early Islamic Civilisation — Baghdad & Silk Roads (c. AD 750–1258)
disclaimer: The History Revision Hub — Key Stage 2 Primary History Mind Map.

root.label: Baghdad c. AD 900
root.gloss: Why the circular Round City of Baghdad became a million-citizen world crossroads of rag paper, the House of Wisdom, algebra, free hospitals, and Silk Road trade.

children.label: 1. Baghdad & House of Wisdom
children.gloss: Caliph al-Mansur built the circular Round City of Peace on the River Tigris, where Samarkand rag paper and multi-faith translators powered the House of Wisdom.

children.label: 1. Building the Round City
children.q2Chain: Caliph al-Mansur picks River Tigris crossroads (762) → 100,000 builders raise circular City of Peace → Million citizens dwarf Saxon towns
children.gloss: Caliph al-Mansur picks River Tigris crossroads (762) → 100,000 builders raise circular City of Peace → Million citizens dwarf Saxon towns

children.label: Choosing the River Tigris Bend
children.gloss: In AD 762, Abbasid Caliph al-Mansur picked a fertile bend on the River Tigris linked by deep canals to the Euphrates.

children.label: Abbasids Needed Central Crossroads
children.gloss: Islam spread swiftly from Arabia; Canals linked Tigris to Euphrates.

children.label: Date Palms, Quffas & Caravans
children.gloss: Round reed quffa boats floated; Silk Road camel caravans met.

children.label: → Funded Planned Brick Capital
children.gloss: Grew lush dates and wheat; Gathered 100,000 skilled builders.

children.label: 100,000 Build City of Peace
children.gloss: Tracing a 2km circle in flaming cotton seeds, 100,000 builders raised double brick walls around the Great Mosque and Green Dome.

children.label: 2km Circle & Double Brick Walls
children.gloss: Traced circle in flaming seeds; Named Madinat al-Salam: Peace.

children.label: Four Iron Gates & Green Dome
children.gloss: Kufa, Basra, Khorasan, Syria gates; Great Mosque stood at heart.

children.label: → Boomed Into 1-Million City
children.gloss: Markets spread beyond round walls; Drew scholars from wide lands.

children.label: 1 Million People vs Britain
children.gloss: By AD 900, Baghdad held nearly one million citizens along paved streets and libraries while Anglo-Saxon London held under 10,000.

children.label: Paved Streets, Canals & Libraries
children.gloss: Home to nearly one million; Bathhouses and shady public gardens.

children.label: Saxon Towns Held 5,000–10,000
children.gloss: London, Winchester had timber huts; Muddy lanes with thatched roofs.

children.label: World’s Largest Learning Hub
children.gloss: Hundred times bigger than Winchester; Powered Golden Age book boom.

children.label: 2. Paper & House of Wisdom
children.q2Chain: Samarkand rag paper sparks 100+ bookshops → Muslim, Christian & Jewish translators rescue scrolls → Fatima al-Fihri & Queen Zubayda
children.gloss: Samarkand rag paper sparks 100+ bookshops → Muslim, Christian & Jewish translators rescue scrolls → Fatima al-Fihri & Queen Zubayda

children.label: Rag Paper & 100+ Bookshops
children.gloss: Caliphs Harun al-Rashid and al-Ma’mun grew the House of Wisdom as cheap cotton-rag paper from Samarkand filled 100+ bookshops.

children.label: European Calfskin Cost Whole Herds
children.gloss: Learned Chinese craft via Samarkand; Watermills beat cotton, linen rags.

children.label: Bayt al-Hikma & Paper Market
children.gloss: Expanded royal House of Wisdom; Over 100 busy Baghdad bookshops.

children.label: → Made Copying Scrolls Affordable
children.gloss: Shared star charts and poetry; Fuelled massive Translation Movement.

children.label: Translators & Hunayn ibn Ishaq
children.gloss: Muslim, Christian, and Jewish scholars like Hunayn ibn Ishaq translated Greek, Persian, and Sanskrit scrolls into Arabic and tested claims.

children.label: Multi-Faith Scholars Worked Together
children.gloss: Muslim, Christian, and Jewish thinkers; Turned Greek, Sanskrit into Arabic.

children.label: Hunayn Tested & Fixed Mistakes
children.gloss: Paid book’s weight in gold; Never copied old claims blindly.

children.label: → Sparked Fresh Science & Maths
children.gloss: Shared one clear Arabic language; Rescued rare crumbling ancient scrolls.

children.label: Fatima al-Fihri & Queen Zubayda
children.gloss: Visionary women patrons funded lasting works: Fatima al-Fihri founded Fez’s al-Qarawiyyin college (AD 859) and Queen Zubayda dug Hajj wells.

children.label: AD 859: Fez College Founded
children.gloss: Fatima al-Fihri funded al-Qarawiyyin; Students still study there today.

children.label: Zubayda’s Desert Hajj Road Wells
children.gloss: Dug stone wells toward Mecca; Saved thousands of thirsty pilgrims.

children.label: Women Patrons Shaped Golden Age
children.gloss: Funded colleges and desert water; Spread learning across Islamic lands.

children.label: 2. Science, Hospitals & Trade
children.gloss: Scholars pioneered 0–9 numerals, algebra, astrolabes, light optics, and free hospitals while camel caravans, dhows, and silver dirhams reached Viking Britain.

children.label: 3. Zero, Optics & Hospitals
children.q2Chain: Al-Khwarizmi’s 0–9 numerals, algebra & astrolabes → Ibn al-Haytham’s camera obscura & free bimaristans → Al-Razi & Al-Zahrawi heal patients
children.gloss: Al-Khwarizmi’s 0–9 numerals, algebra & astrolabes → Ibn al-Haytham’s camera obscura & free bimaristans → Al-Razi & Al-Zahrawi heal patients

children.label: Zero, Algebra & Astrolabes
children.gloss: Al-Khwarizmi championed 0–9 numerals and algebra, Mariam al-Asturlabi crafted brass astrolabes, and al-Jazari built water clocks.

children.label: 0–9 Sifr, Algebra & Algorithms
children.gloss: Beat clumsy Roman numeral sums; Book al-Jabr gave word algebra.

children.label: Brass Astrolabes & Elephant Clock
children.gloss: Mapped stars to find Mecca; Al-Jazari built Elephant Water Clock.

children.label: → Powered Precise Lab Experiments
children.gloss: Cymbals clashed every half hour; Helped scientists measure real nature.

children.label: Camera Obscura & Bimaristans
children.gloss: Ibn al-Haytham proved light travels in straight lines into our eyes using a pinhole room, while free bimaristans treated rich and poor.

children.label: Pinhole Room Proved Straight Light
children.gloss: Busted old Greek eye-ray myth; Inspired modern glasses and cameras.

children.label: Free Bimaristan Wards & Pharmacy
children.gloss: Treated rich and poor free; Gave clean clothes, pocket money.

children.label: → Trained Master Ward Surgeons
children.gloss: Cool fountains calmed clean wards; Let doctors study diseases closely.

children.label: Doctors Al-Razi & Al-Zahrawi
children.gloss: Al-Razi hung fresh meat to pick Baghdad’s cleanest air and told measles from smallpox, while al-Zahrawi drew 200 surgical tools.

children.label: Al-Razi’s Clean-Air Hospital Test
children.gloss: Picked spot meat rotted slowest; Told measles apart from smallpox.

children.label: 200 Tools & Dissolving Stitches
children.gloss: Forceps, scalpels, delicate bone saws; Catgut stitches dissolved inside wounds.

children.label: Guided Medicine for Centuries
children.gloss: Nurses served healthy ward meals; Taught surgeons across Islamic Spain.

children.label: 4. Caravans, Dhows & Coins
children.q2Chain: Silk Road camels & walled caravanserais → Indian Ocean dhows & paper sakk cheques → Silver dirhams in Jorvik & Offa’s gold dinar
children.gloss: Silk Road camels & walled caravanserais → Indian Ocean dhows & paper sakk cheques → Silver dirhams in Jorvik & Offa’s gold dinar

children.label: Souks & Walled Caravanserais
children.gloss: Two-humped camel caravans crossed Silk Road deserts, resting safely every 30 km inside walled caravanserai inns.

children.label: Silk, Porcelain & Spiced Souks
children.gloss: Pepper, cinnamon, Persian woven rugs; Two-humped camels trekked desert trails.

children.label: Walled Caravanserais Every 30 km
children.gloss: Locked brick gates blocked bandits; Cool wells refreshed tired camels.

children.label: → Linked Desert Trails to Basra
children.gloss: Merchants shared stews by firelight; Connected crates to ocean ships.

children.label: Ocean Dhows & Paper Cheques
children.gloss: Coconut-stitched wooden dhows sailed from Basra across the Indian Ocean while bankers invented signed paper sakk slips (cheques).

children.label: Stitched Dhows Sailed by Stars
children.gloss: Planks stitched with coconut rope; Triangular sails; brass star astrolabes.

children.label: Signed Paper Sakk Beat Pirates
children.gloss: Cashed paper slips safely afar; Gave English our word cheque.

children.label: → Silver Coins Flowed to Britain
children.gloss: Sailed toward India and China; Poured silver up Russian rivers.

children.label: Jorvik Hoards & Offa’s Coin
children.gloss: Pure Abbasid silver dirhams were buried in Viking hoards near York, and Anglo-Saxon King Offa of Mercia copied an Arabic gold dinar.

children.label: Arabic Dirhams Buried Near York
children.gloss: Vikings traded furs for silver; Buried dirham hoards near Jorvik.

children.label: AD 774: Offa’s Gold Arabic Coin
children.gloss: King Offa ruled Saxon Mercia; Copied swirling Abbasid Arabic script.

children.label: Proved Trade Reached Britain
children.gloss: Trusted pure coins across continents; Linked Baghdad straight to England.

children.label: 3. Daily Art, 1258 & Legacy
children.gloss: Windcatcher courtyards, geometric tilework, and shatranj chess graced daily Baghdad, and even after Hulagu Khan’s 1258 siege, Cairo, Córdoba, and Toledo saved its ideas.

children.label: 5. Courtyards, Tiles & Chess
children.q2Chain: Windcatcher courtyards & clean hammams → Citrus orchards & geometric mosque tiles → Silk tiraz, lustreware & shatranj chess
children.gloss: Windcatcher courtyards & clean hammams → Citrus orchards & geometric mosque tiles → Silk tiraz, lustreware & shatranj chess

children.label: Windcatchers & Clean Hammams
children.gloss: Tall rooftop badgir windcatchers scooped cool breezes into fountain courtyards while public hammams kept bathers clean with soap.

children.label: Scorching Iraqi Summer Afternoon Heat
children.gloss: Thick brick walls shaded courtyards; Badgirs scooped cool breeze indoors.

children.label: Steamed Hammams & Olive-Oil Soap
children.gloss: Washed clean before daily prayers; Scrubbed with soap and rosewater.

children.label: → Healthy Clean City Neighbourhoods
children.gloss: Tiled hot and cool bathhouses; Fountains cooled orange-tree courtyards.

children.label: Citrus Kitchens & Star Tiles
children.gloss: Canal waterwheels fed lemon, orange, and spinach orchards while mosque artists created geometric stars, arabesque vines, and calligraphy.

children.label: Lemons, Oranges & Cane Sugar
children.gloss: Grew spinach, aubergines, sweet almonds; Served stews on shiny lustreware.

children.label: Geometric Stars & Calligraphy
children.gloss: Avoided statues inside holy mosques; Eight-pointed stars and arabesque vines.

children.label: → Inspired Silk, Glass & Games
children.gloss: Sacred Qur’an script framed walls; Shaped fine workshop craft styles.

children.label: Silk Tiraz, Lamps & Shatranj
children.gloss: Royal looms wove silk tiraz bands, glassblowers gilded mosque lamps, and evening guests cried “Shah mat” playing shatranj chess.

children.label: Silk Tiraz & Glass Mosque Lamps
children.gloss: Embroidered Arabic name bands; Gilded enamelled lamps glowed.

children.label: Shatranj Chess & “Checkmate!”
children.gloss: Sipped sweet rosewater fruit syrups; Shah mat gave word checkmate.

children.label: Dazzling Culture Admired Worldwide
children.gloss: Played evening strategy on carpets; Spread chess across medieval Europe.

children.label: 6. 1258 Siege & Living Ideas
children.q2Chain: Hulagu Khan’s trebuchets breach Baghdad (Feb 1258) → Cairo, Córdoba & Toledo save books in Latin → 0–9 maths, cameras & Arabic words today
children.gloss: Hulagu Khan’s trebuchets breach Baghdad (Feb 1258) → Cairo, Córdoba & Toledo save books in Latin → 0–9 maths, cameras & Arabic words today

children.label: AD 1258: Mongol Siege of Baghdad
children.gloss: After the Abbasid Empire split into weaker states, Hulagu Khan’s Mongol army smashed Baghdad’s brick walls with trebuchets in February 1258.

children.label: Empire Split & Borders Weakened
children.gloss: Rival kingdoms divided Abbasid strength; Hulagu Khan surrounded both banks.

children.label: Trebuchets Breached Walls Feb 1258
children.gloss: Hurled heavy boulders at bricks; Burned palaces, canals, Wisdom library.

children.label: → Ended Caliphate Yet Books Lived
children.gloss: Ended Abbasid rule in Baghdad; Paper copies survived in Spain.

children.label: Cairo, Córdoba & Toledo Bridge
children.gloss: Paper copies sat safely in Cairo, Damascus, and 70-library Córdoba, while Toledo’s multi-faith translators turned Arabic science into Latin.

children.label: Cairo, Córdoba & Alhambra Saved
children.gloss: Copies safe in Cairo, Samarkand; Córdoba shone with seventy libraries.

children.label: Toledo Translated Science to Latin
children.gloss: Muslim, Jewish, Christian team worked; Translated al-Khwarizmi and Ibn Sina.

children.label: → Helped Spark Europe’s Renaissance
children.gloss: Built Granada’s carved Alhambra palace; Carried science into European schools.

children.label: Arabic Maths & Words Today
children.gloss: Every time we write 0–9, snap a phone photo, visit clean hospital wards, or say zero, sugar, lemon, or sofa, Baghdad’s legacy lives on.

children.label: 0–9 Digits, Cameras & Wards
children.gloss: Algebra and phone algorithms daily; Optics led to smartphone cameras.

children.label: Zero, Sugar, Lemon, Orange, Sofa
children.gloss: Everyday words chemistry and cotton; Arrived through busy Arabic trade.

children.label: Books & Ideas Outlasted Empires
children.gloss: Walls fell in February 1258; Shared knowledge still shapes classrooms.
